To me this is uncomfortable as a reality because in some ways it lowers the threshold of failure to a point where it is possible to have absolutely no influence on anything whatsoever and be totally without agency in the carrying out of your life and yet still believe yourself to be free.

I like the phrase "The most evil thing the devil is capable of is to convince you that he doesn't exist." This ties into my thoughts on free will insofar as, if one believes themselves to have free will then there is little difference between having it or not. I bike, do some core exercises (planks and crunches). Yoga and stretches seems to help when I am trying to increase my mileage. For me anything under 30mpw cross training doesn't seem to help at all. When trying to push past 45mpw I think it helps.

I always wondered what is cross training... is it supplemental or substituting to running?

Either way... I think both help "prevent" injuries in different ways.

Supplementary (on-top-of) things like rock climbing, weight lifting, aerobics, zumba, yoga, help strengthen different muscle groups that are typically not used in running, so that a sudden trauma happens (rolled ankle, fall, bump) you will be less likely to hurt something.

Substitution things (instead-of) like cycling, swimming, hiking, elliptical, can also help reduce over training the pounding on the legs when you are trying to increase your cardio and stay off your feet for a bit. That said, you still need to be accustomed to the duration of your race/event you are training for to avoid a world of hurt on race day.

Mostly body-weight exercises like pushups, crunches, lunges, squats, planks, bridges, etc. I'll also use a resistance band when I want to add "weight" to exercises like curls, triceps, etc. As for preventing injuries, meh, not really sure. I know when I did balance work (like on a BOSU), it really helped me keep steady on the trails. And my strength work helped when I needed to climb hills or jump over fallen trees. As for preventing injury though, not really sure. Most of my injuries have been because I did something stupid like trip and fall.
